items.title: --version and --help exit 0; --help lists every command and the exit codes
No arguments, an unknown command or an unknown argument is a usage error with exit code 2 that names the problem
doctor checks that a data folder exists and prints no path
plan prints what a run would build, per world and level, as text or JSON, with or without every block
heightmap writes a 16-bit north-up PGM of one world and refuses to write inside a git working tree
generate builds the far view from flags or from a request document and reports counts per kind
schema <name> prints the published schema of a contract; a missing or unknown name is a usage error
Options are read in any place; --data is required where a command needs it; a load order file combines with --plugin
probe reports numbers about one file (a NIF, a DDS or a flat file) and never a byte of its content
A document names its contract and schema version; a reader refuses another name or an unsupported version
Each contract's JSON schema is committed under schemas/, equals the generated one and is printed by lodwright schema
A reader ignores keys it does not know
A value an open enum does not know reads as other
lodwright contracts --json and --version --json list every contract this build emits and its versions
The plan document lists the worlds, the blocks and the capabilities of this build
The result document carries the status, the counts and the exit code that follows the status
A request document drives a run; omitted fields take their defaults and each bad value is refused with its name
A default request keeps the digest it was released with, wherever the data folder is
An option added after 0.4.2 is optional, is not written while it holds its default and then changes no digest
Digests are SHA-256 over length-prefixed parts, so a different split gives a different digest
The manifest lists every file with its size and digest, sorted, and round-trips
The verify document names its contract and version and reads back
lodwright defaults --json lists every request option with its default, range, tier and the release that added it, read from the code that applies them
With --json the result or the error document goes to stdout, never to stderr, and holds no data path or plugin content
generate --events writes one JSON line per finished block, terrain first, then objects, then trees
A block line names its kind (terrain, objects, trees); a line without one is a terrain block
Every event carries run-wide numbers: run_total is 10000 and run_done never decreases
The library reports each step and block through a Progress callback and stops at a cancel token
A terrain block NIF has the measured eight blocks, vertices, triangles, mirrored UVs, a height per vertex and the block origin, and reads back
An object block NIF has its seven blocks, a segment table covering the triangles and one texture set per shape, and reads back
Reading what was written gives the same file, writing what was read gives the same bytes, and unknown blocks survive byte for byte
A truncated, corrupt or inconsistent NIF is a typed error, never a panic, and an inconsistent block cannot be written
DDS files are written as BC1, BC3 or BC5 with a mip chain and the documented header, never with a DX10 header
Encoding then decoding keeps a quality floor for BC1, BC3 and BC5 on gradients and noise
DDS files are read: BC1, BC3, BC5, BC7 with a DX10 header block by block, and uncompressed 32-bit through its masks
A bad header, a size over the cap, random bytes or a bit flip is a typed error, never a panic
Mip chains halve rounding down to one pixel; box and Lanczos resizing are the same bytes at any thread count
Plugins are read: header, masters, group tree, compressed records, extended subrecords, worlds, cells, land, land textures and placed references
A truncated, corrupt or absurdly nested plugin is a typed error, never a panic
Plugin headers are read for master order; a master after its dependent is an error
BSA version 104 archives are read, compressed or not, and looked up by name in any case and separator
A truncated or corrupt archive, or one claiming huge sizes, is refused without allocating or panicking
Version 104 archives are written with the game's name hashes, records in hash order and no embedded names; the same bytes at any thread count
A path the format cannot hold, two names with one hash, a file over 1 GiB or an archive over 4 GiB is refused with its reason
An archive extracts below one folder only, removes the folder when dropped and leaves none when the archive is bad
A loose file beats an archive; a later plugin's archive beats an earlier one; the override marker lets a later archive replace
The stub plugin has no record, one master and the archive's base name, and is the same bytes every time
Each world's terrain step gets as many workers as the budget leaves room for, never fewer than one
A run under a low budget writes the same files and the same manifest as one without
A run whose plugins alone suggest more than the budget is refused as memory_limit before anything is read
A run over sixty worlds stays under its budget: worlds are walked one at a time
The result reports the peak memory where the platform says (Linux)
A memory cap option bounds the whole run, not only the terrain workers
An output folder that is not empty and has no manifest is refused unless --overwrite is given
An output folder inside the data folder, or a link into it, is refused
An output folder in a git working tree, or a link into one, is refused
A link below the output folder is refused and nothing is written through it; a link at a file's path is replaced, never followed
An output folder that is a link to a separate folder is written through and stays up to date
A manifest that lists an absolute path or one with .. is not trusted and never makes a run remove a file outside the output folder
Every file is written to a temporary name and renamed, so a failed write leaves the previous file and no temporary file
Only plain relative paths are written; a path that climbs out of the folder is refused and nothing is written

groups.title: Packing the output into an archive

items.title: output.pack leaves one BSA archive, a stub plugin, an empty override marker and the manifest, and nothing loose
The pack switch changes neither the request digest nor a block digest
A packed output is up to date when the archive, the stub and the marker are intact; a changed archive is rebuilt
Switching the option off builds the loose files again and the output never holds both forms
A packing step that fails leaves the loose output as it was, with no spool and no temporary file
The archive is the same bytes at any thread count
A pack phase sits between the last world and the manifest and the run total never goes back
Only object and tree textures are stored compressed; a file listed by several worlds is packed once
An archive extracted again is the same files and verifies clean; damage made before packing is found
Packing is the default output form
A run writes the far view and a manifest
A run with an unchanged request and unchanged plugins answers up to date and writes nothing
An output written by another version or another build is rebuilt, not reported up to date
Terrain blocks whose inputs did not change are kept; the others are built
Files the old manifest listed that the new run neither kept nor wrote are removed
Object and tree blocks are rebuilt in full whenever a run is not up to date
Object and tree blocks are reused when their inputs did not change
The output files are the same bytes at any thread count
A thread count on the command line replaces the one in the request file
A load order file lists the plugins; comments, blank lines and active markers are skipped; plugin names match in any case
The inputs digest follows the plugin contents and not the folder they are in
A run with warnings leaves lodwright-warnings.json beside the manifest, one record per plugin and kind
The result's own warning list holds at most twenty lines and the last line counts the rest
A failure is a typed error with a stable code and a copy text that holds no command line
The result profiles every step with its time and the files it wrote
A run builds into <output>.lodwright-staging and replaces the output folder only when every step has finished
A cancelled run leaves the previous output untouched
A run killed over an existing output leaves that output untouched
The next run resumes a cancelled run from its checkpoint and writes what an uninterrupted run writes
A killed run resumes to the bytes of an uninterrupted run
A staging folder of another request or other inputs, or without a checkpoint, is removed and the run starts clean
A swap killed between its two renames is put back by the next run
A file the user keeps at the top of the output folder survives a regenerate
A run that cannot fit is refused before building, with output_no_space
A lock refuses two runs on one output folder
A swap marker tells the next run which half of a swap it finds
Files, the checkpoint and the folders are synced before the swap
Objects are merged per block with their transform, scale and atlas UVs
Object blocks start at the grid anchor and follow the game's tree
Textures are packed into a BC3 atlas with a half-size normal atlas, deterministically and without overlap
Textures that do not fit one atlas keep their size on further numbered pages, each with its own shape
A UV outside its texture is held at the edge, not wrapped to the far edge
A block over the 16-bit vertex or triangle limit is written as several shapes and nothing is left out
objects.drop_under_terrain and objects.drop_under_water leave out faces that cannot be seen and count them
A model's own LOD model is read, also when bytes follow its footer, and takes the full model's texture when it has none
An uncompressed 32-bit texture is used as it is, not replaced by a flat colour
A missing or unreadable model, and an absent or undecodable texture, are named in warnings of their own kind
Nothing is written when no model can be read and the output is deterministic
objects.shapes_from_shipped_blocks takes a model's far shape from the blocks the games ship, in the world a rule names
objects.shapes_from_full_models draws objects without a LOD model with a simplified copy of their full model, and reports them
A rule gives a far shape to the models it names and to no other; its limits win over the switch
A model that is see-through, or drawn without lighting, gets no far shape
The simplifier keeps the requested share of triangles within an error limit, keeps seams closed and locked borders, and gives the same output on every system
Trees are drawn as impostors by the engine

groups.title: Which objects enter the far view

items.title: Only statics flagged visible when distant become instances; the plugin that sets the flag is the one that counts
High Priority LOD is read from the base object as well as the reference; bit 16 on an activator is not it
A reference disabled when the game starts is left out; a persistent one still counts, as in the game's own blocks
A reference follows the start state of its enable parent chain, across worlds and plugins
A reference a later plugin deletes drops out and a third plugin can place it again
A static collection keeps its parts and placements; a collection with parts is not also drawn as its own model
A temporary reference goes to the block of its cell
inclusion rules exclude objects by plugin, record or model glob, and keep only listed plugins
inclusion.include_rules takes objects nothing marks visible from far into object LOD, by model pattern, plugin and record type
An include rule takes a reference by the start state of its enable parent
An include rule's generate option gives far shapes to its objects only
objects.far_model_without_flag takes unflagged references that have a far model and stand when the game starts
objects.far_lights writes the steady lights near drawn objects as one marked unlit light-point shape per block
Inclusion rules per plugin apply to terrain cells
Blocks are planned at the four levels 4, 8, 16 and 32 cells; a world gets only the levels its width allows
Each block is meshed by greedy insertion under a height tolerance, from source samples only
A block never has more than 32767 vertices: the tolerance is raised until it fits
Neighbouring blocks share identical vertices along their common edge
Ground without data gets no triangles
Block files are named from the world, level and block coordinates the game's tree uses
The block grid starts at the cell of the world's minimum corner, as the game's own tree does
Skirts under every border vertex close the gap to a neighbouring block of the same or another level
terrain.drop_under_water leaves out terrain faces the water hides
Faces that cannot be seen are hidden (optimize unseen)
Per-block quality is tuned against the game's own blocks
A world with no land writes nothing; a world name that is not a folder name is refused
The diffuse map blends each cell's land texture layers over its base by opacity, in order
A land texture resolves through its texture set, falls back to its icon, and follows a later plugin's override
Normal maps follow the heights; flat ground gives the flat normal and gaps do not poison the map
The default land texture is read from the game's ini
terrain.land_light darkens the composed far land the way the near land is lit
terrain.texture_scales sets how often a land texture repeats; unlisted textures repeat once
terrain.levels[].specular_alpha carries specular in the alpha of the normal maps, written as BC3
terrain.compose_shipped_tiles off: the game's own far-land tile is left to the engine where no mod changed the land
A land texture that is in no folder or archive is its own warning kind and names the path only
One .lod settings file per world, with the world's bounds and block sizes
A cell with ground below its water height gets a flat water plane at that height, unless water is turned off
A cell's water height comes from its record or its world's default
A block of default water at or below zero gets the placeholder shape
terrain.water_walls writes a wall on every border side that has water
At levels 8 to 32 squares of one water height merge into rectangles
terrain.water_shared_vertices writes a corner two rectangles share once
terrain.water_polygons writes the water of a block as traced polygons of the same wet squares
The game's own water outline and sloped edges are reproduced
A land record's VHGT decodes to 33 by 33 heights, exactly for heights on the grid
The heights of a world become one raster of whole blocks with shared edge vertices
A later plugin overrides cells and the world record through its master index
A missing master is reported by name
A world is named by its editor id, or by its form id when it has none
The extent follows the declared corners, and a world with land beyond 128 cells gets the 128-cell window of the game's files
Cells without land inside the extent are flat at the default land height
A child world keeps its own data by default and takes its parent's default heights only when its flag says so and the request asks
Tale of Two Wastelands children resolve their parent through the Fallout 3 master
The seam error between neighbouring cells is measured: zero for matching seams, a step shows
A world gets terrain LOD only with seventeen cells with land and a display name
A world's trees are written as a list file, one block per cell group and one atlas
Tree blocks align to the world corner; cells below it are out of range
Only flagged bases become tree types; hidden or fallen references leave empty blocks
Billboard names use the defining plugin, the model stem and the form id without load index
Identical billboards share one atlas rectangle and the output is repeatable
A DLC4 world uses the swamp atlas; a world without billboards writes nothing
The settings file overrides the bounds only for the sizes it states
The order of trees inside a block is the game's own
verify checks the formats of terrain blocks, object blocks, tree blocks, textures and settings files, and finds damage
verify exits 0 clean, 1 with findings, 2 on a usage error and 3 on an unreadable folder
With --reference, blocks present on both sides are compared by name in lower case
verify measures the water overlap (IoU) of every block with water on either side and fails a block under --water-iou
verify compares terrain heights on a 33 by 33 grid and fails a block over --height-tolerance
verify counts the vertices of an object block with no counterpart in the reference, in any order
verify reports the Pearson correlation of each block's diffuse and normal map with the reference's
verify reports position, UV and silhouette errors of object blocks and the use of each atlas
--known-differences moves listed differences out of the failures and reports a listed path that no longer differs as stale
A report holds file names and numbers only, never content read from a file
verify refuses a folder or reference inside a git working tree unless --allow-in-repo is given for that run
lodwright bands prints the minimum and maximum of every statistic over several verify reports; a zero-width band is an exact match
lodwright landmarks says whether each named landmark is written, missing, excluded, without a far model or unresolved
A landmark baseline passes when nothing is lost and fails when a written landmark is gone
A release passes the checklist on the owner's real data (docs/RELEASE-TEST.md)
Generated blocks load and draw in the game
The terrain block and atlas steps stay within a few times their recorded cost
